core_obligations: Blow up the product of the Fitting ideals Fit_k(F) (a finite product, since Fit_k(F) = O_X for k beyond the number of generators in a local presentation) to obtain a U-admissible blowup b : X' -> X on which every Fit_k(F) is invertible, and reduce to the case where the Fit_k(F) are already invertible (proof lines 13291-13307).

Show that the divisors are forced and locally constructible: with E_k the effective Cartier divisor defined by Fit_k(F) the divisors must satisfy E_k = D_{k+1} + 2 D_{k+2} + 3 D_{k+3} + ..., a locally finite relation that determines the D_k uniquely, so it suffices to construct them locally (proof lines 13308-13317).

Induct on the number n of generators of a local presentation: set D_k = empty for k > n and D_n = E_{n-1}, shrink so that Fit_{n-1} is generated by a nonzerodivisor f, write A = f A', apply the two-ideals blowup input to see that F' has a presentation with n - 1 generators and that f^{n-k} Fit_k(F') = Fit_k(F), and then build the two filtrations of F from the two factorizations A = A'f = f A' of the presentation matrix as the kernel and the cokernel of multiplication by f (proof lines 13319-13363).
proof_roadmap: Blow up the product of the Fitting ideals to make them invertible and note that the blowup is U-admissible (proof lines 13291-13305).
Identify the divisors through the relation E_k = D_{k+1} + 2 D_{k+2} + ... and reduce the construction to a local, finite computation (proof lines 13307-13317).

Induct on the number of generators of a local presentation, factoring the matrix as A = f A' with f a nonzerodivisor, and use the two factorizations as the kernel and cokernel descriptions giving the ascending and descending filtrations with the required rank condition on D_i (proof lines 13319-13363).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts the existence of a U-admissible blowup b : X' -> X, for a perfect O_X-module F of tor dimension <= 1 that vanishes on an open U, together with two canonical locally finite filtrations of F' = b^*F whose successive quotients F^i/F^{i-1} and F_i/F_{i+1} are finite locally free of rank i on an effective Cartier divisor D_i (statement lines 13265-13288). The proof has to construct the blowup and the divisors simultaneously: it blows up the product of all Fitting ideals Fit_k(F) (which is a finite product because Fit_k(F) = O_X for k past the number of generators in a local presentation), then uses the invertibility of Fitting ideals after blowing up to reduce to the case where each Fit_k(F) is invertible, where the divisors must satisfy the chain of equalities E_k = D_{k+1} + 2 D_{k+2} + 3 D_{k+3} + ... and are therefore determined uniquely (proof lines 13291-13317). The induction on the number n of generators then replaces the matrix A = f A' by A' with f a nonzerodivisor generating Fit_{n-1}, uses f^{n-k} Fit_k(F') = Fit_k(F)|_V, and finally produces the two filtrations from the two factorizations A = A'f = f A' as the kernel and cokernel of multiplication by f (proof lines 13319-13363). The simultaneous determination of the divisors by the Fitting ideals and the canonical kernel/cokernel description of the two filtrations are not a routine consequence of an existing theorem, so the claim is H3.
